-118.46300,34.04730.name: California Fertility Partners
-118.46300,34.04730.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Richard P. Marrs, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-2.21583,53.39728.name: Aurora Reproductive Healthcare
-2.21583,53.39728.state: The Alexandra Hospital, Mill Lane, Cheadle, SK8 2PX
-2.21583,53.39728.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to Manchester Fertility. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-71.06919,42.33593.name: National Emerging Infectious Disease Laboratories (NEIDL)
-71.06919,42.33593.state: 620 Albany Street, Boston, MA 02118, United States
-71.06919,42.33593.desc: A BSL4 animal laboratory, operational. Run by Boston University. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in full-body positive-pressure suits with their own air supply. Containment space: 1,202 SqM. Operational or announced: 2017. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-71.04500,42.34400.name: Vertex / CRISPR Therapeutics — Casgevy
-71.04500,42.34400.desc: The first CRISPR therapy approved anywhere, for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia, listed at over two million dollars per patient. The scientific credit sits with the academic founders; the pricing decision sits here. Sickle cell is overwhelmingly a West African and Indian disease, and the cure for it was built for American insurance — which decides who gets fixed before any laboratory work begins.

-71.04500,42.34400.name: Vertex Pharmaceuticals
-71.04500,42.34400.desc: Holds commercial control of Casgevy, the first approved CRISPR therapy, developed with CRISPR Therapeutics. Vertex is the partner that took it through approval and sets the price, and its earlier cystic fibrosis franchise is the template: a small patient population, an extremely high price, and a payer system reorganised around a single company's product. The same model applied to a curable genetic disease is what the sickle cell rollout is now testing.
